title: Review
intro: Sins and tawbah, Asr, the traveller’s prayer, Isha and witr – let’s repeat what we learned.

learn.html: Let’s repeat what we have learned about sins and tawbah, the Asr and Isha prayers, witr and the prayer of a traveller (musafir). Read each part, try to say it in your own words, then do the activities.
In your notebook, finish each sentence: A sin is… · Small sins are… · Serious sins are… · Tawbah is… · A musafir is…

items: Small sins include talking while the adhan is being called and missing the prayer in jama‘ah without a good reason.
A major sin is what is clearly forbidden in the Qur’an, with a punishment in this world and the next.
Of all kinds of sin, only the serious sins take a person out of Islam.

Serious sins: kufr – disbelief in Allah and the basic truths of faith, and denying them; shirk – associating partners with Allah; riddah – leaving Islam; nifaq – hypocrisy in faith; mocking, ridiculing and insulting holy things; denying the fard and the haram.
Allah forbade sins because they cause harm in both worlds.

learn.title: ⭐ Accepting tawbah
learn.html: For tawbah to be accepted, a person stops the sin, regrets it in the heart and does not go back to it. Telling other people about the sin is not one of the conditions.

items: Asr has 8 rak‘ahs: 4 sunnah and 4 fard. The fard of Asr is prayed the same way as the fard of Dhuhr.
In the sunnah of Asr, in the first sitting we recite At-Tahiyyat and the salawat, and in the 3rd rak‘ah we start again with Subhanaka, A‘udhu, Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah.
Isha has 13 rak‘ahs: 4 sunnah, 4 fard, 2 last sunnah and 3 witr. The first sunnah of Isha is prayed like the sunnah of Asr.

Witr – 1st rak‘ah: Subhanaka, A‘udhu, Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah. 2nd rak‘ah: Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah. First sitting: At-Tahiyyat. 3rd rak‘ah: Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah, then after a takbir the Qunut dua.
A traveller does not have to pray the sunnah prayers, and shortens the fard of four rak‘ahs to two.
A traveller prays in a vehicle only if it cannot stop for a break.
The easing counts if the stay away lasts up to 15 days. If he intends to stay longer, it counts only while he is still on the way.
A traveller may lead people who are not travelling as their imam.

learn.html: Practise: Build the Salah – the Asr and Isha levels, and the Qunut dua.

questions.q: How many rak‘ahs does Asr have?
What easing does a musafir (traveller) use?
options: He does not have to pray the sunnah, and shortens the fard
He shortens both the sunnah and the fard
He leaves the fard and shortens the sunnah

questions.q: The first sunnah of Isha is prayed the same way as the sunnah of…
How many rak‘ahs does Isha have, with witr?
When do we recite the Qunut dua?
options: In the 3rd rak‘ah of witr, after a takbir
In the 3rd rak‘ah of the Isha sunnah
In the first sitting of Asr

questions.q: Which sins take a person out of Islam?

practice.title: True or false?
practice.prompt: Is the sentence true or false?

items.text: We wipe away small sins by doing good deeds and by tawbah.
A person who commits a major sin is still a Muslim.
A person who commits a serious sin stops being a Muslim.
Sin harms a person’s mental and physical health.
A person can become rich by sinning.
Those who sin weaken the community.
Someone who sins does not need to ask Allah for forgiveness.
Damage done by a sin must be made good.
Asr time lasts from when the sun leans to the west until full darkness.
The fard of Asr and the fard of Dhuhr are prayed differently.
Isha time lasts from sunset until Fajr.
A traveller may be the imam for people who are not travelling.
We recite the Qunut dua in the 3rd rak‘ah of the Isha sunnah.

practice.title: A serious sin or not?
practice.prompt: Does this person commit a serious sin – one that takes a person out of Islam?
bins: ⚠️ Not a serious sin (but still a sin)

items.text: Mushrik – associates partners with Allah
Kafir – disbelieves in Allah
Someone who leaves Islam
Munafiq – a hypocrite in faith
Someone who does not fast
A smoker
Someone who drinks alcohol

practice.title: Conditions for tawbah
practice.prompt: Tap every condition for tawbah to be accepted, then tap Check.

options.text: Never do the same sin again
Tell other people about the sin
options.why: Tawbah is between you and Allah – we don’t need to tell others about our sins.

practice.title: Isha in order
practice.prompt: Put the parts of Isha in order.

practice.title: In your notebook
prompts: 📋 Define: a sin, small sins, serious sins, tawbah, a musafir.
📋 Write the order of the 4 sunnah rak‘ahs of Asr – what do we recite in each rak‘ah and sitting?

✏️ Cross out the odd one out among the major sins: taking a life, disobeying elders, disobeying parents, quarrelling, lying, two-facedness, betting, backbiting. Talk about your answer with your muallim.
